look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · Slender UNARMED scrambling or clump-forming plant with often sharply TRIANGULAR / HASTATE leaves and three-angled green stems. Tiny WHITE (sometimes violet-tinged) five-lobed star flowers have roughly equal SEPARATE yellow anthers and occasionally a shiny green/white eye at the corolla base. Flower clusters usually 3–6. Fruits eventually BRIGHT RED (some local treatments describe dark red to almost black), but NO VERIFIED RIPE-FRUIT PHOTO IS PRESENT in this card. The chief look-alike is introduced bittersweet nightshade (S. dulcamara): usually purple swept-back flowers with more joined anthers and larger branching flower clusters; white dulcamara forms exist. Do not ID on berry color alone.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Solanaceae/Solanum: alternate leaves, 5-parted rotate/stellate corollas, poricidal anthers, and berry fruits.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Unarmed, thin-stemmed scrambling or ascending herb/subshrub; basal stems may be woody; stems often sharply three-angled / ridged.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Simple ALTERNATE leaves, often narrow triangular / hastate with basal pointed or rounded lobes, but leaf shape can vary greatly even on one plant.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: WHITE or occasionally purple-tinted star corolla with five pointed lobes and shiny green or greenish-white corolla eye; the eye may require a macro.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Yellow anthers nearly equal and individually FREE rather than joined into a tube; FNA reports ~3.5–4 mm.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Small usually 3–6-flowered, unbranched or lightly forked cymes; fruit/flower pedicels insert into little sleeves on inflorescence axis.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Ripening to shiny RED berries (FNA ~10–15 mm), though local botanical descriptions include dark red/black fruit. Mature fruit NOT yet represented by a photo in gallery.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Cannot confirm anther pores, eye spots, or fully mature berry just from current Joey field photographs.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Semiwoody scrambling vine-like herb or subshrub, up to 2 m in FNA (Williamson County specimens often lower). Slender three-angled ridged unarmed shoots; may climb or thread through other shrubs and fences. Not a twining vine in the narrow structural sense.

key_traits.label: Stems
key_traits.text: Green often distinctly angled/ridged, unarmed (no prickles); at least two ridges may descend from leaf nodes. Woody towards base in older plants.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Simple alternate triangular, deltate or hastate, sometimes mostly narrow linear and sometimes basally 2-lobed. Typical FNA ~1.8–5 cm long but variable; do NOT use leaf outline by itself.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Usually small WHITE five-part stars, sometimes faint purple; green or green-white shiny eye at bases of corolla lobes (may be hard to see in these photos). Yellow anthers equal and FREE (not fused/cone), ~3.5–4 mm in FNA. Poricidal anthers may eventually open into slits, but terminal pores NOT resolved in current photos.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Often unbranched or forked terminal/leaf-opposed 3–6-flowered cyme; pedicels inserted into sleeves and may droop with open flower. Compare introduced S. dulcamara's larger 7–40-flowered many-branched inflorescence.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Shiny red berry usually ~1–1.5 cm in FNA, unlike black berries of Morelloid group; some central Texas reference material documents berries dark red to black and smaller. Color varies—obtain vouchered ripe local fruit photographs before teaching colors as absolute.

lookalikes.differences: KEY LOOK-ALIKE: S. dulcamara also scrambles, may have hastate leaves, green-eyed flowers and RED fruits. S. triquetrum has smaller 3–6 flower clusters, sharply angled stems, usually WHITE corolla and anthers free/individually distinct. S. dulcamara normally has larger 7–40-flowered branched clusters and reflexed PURPLE lobes (rare white forms). Black-berried American/European morelloids are generally herbs with different reproductive characters.
